speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the rash first appeared and whether it started on your trunk before spreading to your extremities? Also, have you noticed any blisters or a "dewdrop on a rose petal" appearance to the lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the facial rash sparing the mouth is a significant clue. Has the rash on her trunk and extremities appeared as flat, red spots or as raised, scaly patches? Also, has she had any recent contact with children who have had chickenpox or a similar rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the mouth, followed by the trunk and extremity rash, is highly suggestive of a specific viral exanthem. To confirm this, I need to check the nature of the lesions; are the spots on her body flat red spots or raised bumps, and do they feel rough to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the classic "slapped cheek" rash sparing the mouth followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).
